How EDFM handles redirects and, eventually, disambiguation.

== When to create a redirect ==
* Common abbreviations and initialisms (e.g. <code>BGS</code> → [[Background Simulation]]).
* American/British spelling variants (e.g. <code>Colonization</code> → [[Colonisation]]).
* Predictable alternate phrasing a commander might actually type (e.g. <code>New Player Guide</code> → [[New Commander Roadmap]]).
* Common short forms of a proper name (e.g. <code>Farseer</code> → [[Felicity Farseer]]).

Do '''not''' create a redirect for a guessed misspelling nobody has actually been observed to type, or "just in case" — every redirect is a small ongoing maintenance surface, not a free action.

== Hard rule: the target must exist ==
A redirect's target page must already exist. Never create a redirect that points at a page that hasn't been written yet — that's a disguised red link, and defeats the purpose of {{tl|Article status}}'s honesty about what's actually here. <code>Special:BrokenRedirects</code> is the audit tool for catching any that slip through or whose target later gets renamed/deleted.

== Disambiguation ==
No title collision currently exists anywhere on EDFM. When one first happens (two different subjects that would naturally share a title), follow the standard parenthetical pattern: <code>Foo (context)</code> for each specific meaning, with a plain <code>Foo</code> page becoming either the more common/primary meaning (with a hatnote pointing to the other) or a short <code>Foo (disambiguation)</code>-style list once there are 3 or more meanings. This matches the convention most large wikis in this style (including RuneScape Wiki, EDFM's stated model) already use, rather than inventing a new one.

== Mass renames ==
Use the Replace Text extension (already installed) rather than hand-editing every incoming link individually if a page ever needs to move — see Special:ReplaceText.
